messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - It integrates a simple exponential-growth ODE from a very large start time t0 ≈ 1.878250320e9 to an “end event” time tEvent ≈ 1.8782503799999986e9, with a fixed Runge-Kutta 4 integrator and step size 60.0.
  - It expects the integrator to stop exactly at tEvent (within 5e-6).

- How stopping at end time is implemented:
  - RungeKuttaIntegrator.integrate wraps the user’s events with an extra “end-of-range” event by calling addEndTimeChecker(t0, t, eventsHandlersManager) (see AbstractIntegrator.addEndTimeChecker).
  - This builds a new CombinedEventsManager with existing event handlers and adds a new EndTimeChecker for the deadline t.
  - During each tentative step, the integrator:
    - Computes the step end state.
    - Invokes manager.evaluateStep(interpolator).
    - If an event is detected, it retrieves eventTime and computes dt = eventTime - stepStart; otherwise it accepts the full step.

- The critical code path:
  - In RungeKuttaIntegrator.integrate, the event adjustment logic is:
    - interpolator.storeTime(stepStart + stepSize);
    - if (manager.evaluateStep(interpolator)) {
        dt = manager.getEventTime() - stepStart;
        if (Math.abs(dt) <= Math.ulp(stepStart)) {
          // don’t truncate, accept loop end
        } else {
          stepSize = dt;  // adopt event time as the new step size
        }
      } else {
        loop = false; // accept full step
      }
  - There is no check that the new stepSize (dt) remains within the bounds of the original tentative step.

- What goes wrong:
  - The current bug report notes that “numerical accuracy in events detection leads to error in events location” for the end-of-integration event.
  - CombinedEventsManager.evaluateStep is expected to deliver an event time within the current step interval [stepStart, stepStart + stepSize] (forward integration). However, due to numerical inaccuracies when locating the end-of-range event (with very large absolute times), the returned event time can sometimes slightly overshoot the step end.
  - Because RungeKuttaIntegrator.integrate blindly assigns stepSize = dt without constraining it to the current step length, a small overshoot in the located event time can inflate dt beyond the actual step size. The integrator then attempts a much larger step than intended.
  - In the failing scenario, the intended step is 60 seconds, but the erroneous event time leads to dt ≈ 160 seconds. The integrator thus performs a step covering ~160 seconds, missing the designated end time and returning a time far beyond tEvent. This matches the observed failure where the integration range is “more than twice the specified range.”

- Why the test exacerbates the issue:
  - The start and end times are very large (≈ 1.878e9), and the end event lies very close to the tentative step end (tEvent ≈ t0 + 59.9999957). Root-finding on the time-only event function can be sensitive to round-off in this regime.
  - addEndTimeChecker configures the end event with:
    - maxCheckInterval = +∞ (only the whole step is checked), and
    - convergence = Math.ulp(max(|t0|, |tEvent|)) (extremely tight absolute tolerance at that magnitude).
  - This combination makes the event search particularly susceptible to returning a time very slightly beyond the step end due to rounding, which, in the absence of any clamping in the integrator, triggers the step inflation.

- Summary of root cause:
  - RungeKuttaIntegrator.integrate does not validate that the event time reported by CombinedEventsManager.evaluateStep lies within the current step bounds. It directly sets stepSize = (eventTime - stepStart) even if this pushes the end of the step past the original tentative step end.
  - A slight event-location overshoot therefore causes the integrator to take an overlong step (e.g., 160s instead of 60s), missing the intended end-of-range event and failing the test.
